Two decisions change the implementation enough that I should not lock a plan yet.

### Current baseline
- Panel auth: Flask session + username/password in [`relocation_jobs/core/auth.py`](relocation_jobs/core/auth.py), routes in [`relocation_jobs/web/routes/auth.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/auth.py)
- Self-serve register gated by `PANEL_ALLOW_REGISTER`
- Users table has `username` + `password_hash` only (no email / Google subject)
- MCP connector login ([`relocation_jobs/mcp/oauth_pages.py`](relocation_jobs/mcp/oauth_pages.py)) reuses the same password auth
- Design system to follow: [`design.md`](design.md) (Warm Horizon / Kuchup tokens)

### Need your call

**1. Signup model**
- **A.** Self-serve — first Google login creates the user
- **B.** Admin-gated — Google only signs in users an admin already created
- **C.** Self-serve behind an env flag (like `PANEL_ALLOW_REGISTER` today)

**2. Password + MCP**
- **A.** Google for panel **and** MCP; keep password only for `PANEL_ADMIN_*` ops bootstrap
- **B.** Google for panel only; leave MCP password login alone for now
- **C.** Google everywhere; remove password login entirely (including admin)

My recommendation if you want the shortest path to “Google is the tunnel”: **1A + 2A** — self-serve Google for normal users, admin password kept for bootstrap/ops, MCP switches to the same Google identity so connectors stay consistent.

Reply with your choices (e.g. `1A 2A`) and I’ll produce the full implementation plan against the project skills (`engineering-standards`, `module-layout`, `design.md` / Hallmark for the login surface).

input.plan:
# Google-only user registration and login

## Decisions (locked)

| Choice | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Signup | Self-serve on first Google login, gated by `PANEL_ALLOW_REGISTER` (same semantics as today) |
| Password | Removed everywhere — panel, MCP OAuth page, `reset_password`, admin bootstrap password |
| Admin | `PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS` (comma-separated Google emails) → `is_admin` on create/login |

## Current baseline

- Session auth: [`relocation_jobs/core/auth.py`](relocation_jobs/core/auth.py) + [`relocation_jobs/web/routes/auth.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/auth.py)
- UI: username/password form in [`relocation_jobs/static/index.html`](relocation_jobs/static/index.html) / [`relocation_jobs/static/js/auth.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/auth.js)
- Users schema: `username` + `password_hash NOT NULL` in [`relocation_jobs/core/db.py`](relocation_jobs/core/db.py)
- MCP connector login still posts username/password ([`relocation_jobs/mcp/oauth_pages.py`](relocation_jobs/mcp/oauth_pages.py))
- Tests log in via `POST /api/auth/login` ([`tests/conftest.py`](tests/conftest.py) `auth_client`)

## Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Browser
  participant Panel as Flask_panel
  participant Google
  participant DB as users_repo

  Browser->>Panel: GET /api/auth/google
  Panel->>Browser: 302 Google authorize + state
  Browser->>Google: consent
  Google->>Panel: GET /api/auth/google/callback?code&state
  Panel->>Google: exchange code, verify id_token
  Panel->>DB: upsert by google_sub
  Note over Panel,DB: new user only if PANEL_ALLOW_REGISTER
  Panel->>Browser: session cookie, redirect /panel
```

MCP path reuses the same Google verify + upsert, carrying `mcp_request_id` in OAuth `state`, then calls existing `complete_login_redirect`.

## Data model

Migration in [`relocation_jobs/core/migrations.py`](relocation_jobs/core/migrations.py) (and mirror nullable/`CREATE` shape in [`relocation_jobs/core/db.py`](relocation_jobs/core/db.py) for fresh DBs):

- `google_sub TEXT UNIQUE` (stable Google subject)
- `email TEXT UNIQUE` (normalized lower)
- `display_name TEXT`
- `password_hash` → nullable, then stop writing it; drop column in same migration once unused (dead code deletion — no dual-write period)

Repo changes in [`relocation_jobs/users/repo.py`](relocation_jobs/users/repo.py):

- `get_user_by_google_sub`, `get_user_by_email`
- `create_google_user(...)` / `upsert_google_user(...)` — no password
- Delete `update_user_password`
- Username: prefer email local-part; uniquify with numeric suffix on collision

**Legacy rows:** existing password-only users have no `google_sub`. They cannot sign in after cutover until linked. Ops path: set `PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS` to your Gmail; first Google login creates/flags admin. Orphan username-only rows can be deleted manually if unused.

## Auth core (no SQL outside repo)

Rewrite [`relocation_jobs/core/auth.py`](relocation_jobs/core/auth.py):

- Keep: `login_user`, `logout_user`, `login_required`, `admin_required`, `auth_status`, `allow_register`, `init_auth`
- Add: `login_or_register_google(profile)` — upsert; if new and `not allow_register()` → `ValueError`; set `is_admin` from `PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS`
- Remove: `authenticate`, `register_user`, password hashing, `bootstrap_admin` password sync, `sync_admin_password_from_env`
- `init_auth`: no password bootstrap; empty DB is fine until first Google login
- Cookies: keep HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax; set `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` when not localhost

New module [`relocation_jobs/core/google_oauth.py`](relocation_jobs/core/google_oauth.py) (HTTP/crypto only, no SQL):

- Build authorize URL (scopes: `openid email profile`)
- Validate `state` (CSRF)
- Exchange code → tokens
- Verify ID token (`google-auth` / JWKS) against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`
- Return `{google_sub, email, display_name}`

Dependency: add `google-auth` (and `requests` if not already present). No Authlib required.

## HTTP surface

[`relocation_jobs/web/routes/auth.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/auth.py):

| Method | Path | Behavior |
|--------|------|----------|
| GET | `/api/auth/status` | unchanged shape; `allow_register` still exposed |
| POST | `/api/auth/logout` | unchanged |
| GET | `/api/auth/google` | start OAuth (`next` / panel return URL optional) |
| GET | `/api/auth/google/callback` | finish OAuth → session → redirect `/panel` |
| DELETE | `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/register` | remove endpoints |

Update [`tests/helpers/route_manifest.py`](tests/helpers/route_manifest.py) accordingly.

## Panel UI ([`design.md`](design.md))

App login is workbench chrome — function over enrichment; use existing Warm Horizon tokens.

- Replace username/password form with one primary CTA: **Continue with Google** → `/api/auth/google`
- Keep brand lockup; short hint; error region for callback `?error=`
- Remove register toggle / password fields from HTML + JS
- [`auth.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/auth.js): drop `submitAuth` password path; on load honor `error` query; `refreshAuth` unchanged

## MCP OAuth page

[`relocation_jobs/mcp/oauth_pages.py`](relocation_jobs/mcp/oauth_pages.py):

- Replace password form with Continue with Google
- Start Google OAuth with `state` encoding `{nonce, mcp_request_id}` (or session-bound request_id)
- Callback (shared handler or MCP-specific route on the MCP app) verifies Google, `login_or_register_google`, then `complete_login_redirect`
- Align page styling with Kuchup tokens (drop the old green system font card)
- Delete `authenticate` usage

Stdio MCP `MCP_USERNAME` / `MCP_USER_ID` for local agent tooling stays as **user resolution**, not password auth — out of scope to remove unless it breaks.

## Env and ops

[`.env.example`](.env.example), [`docs/operations/ec2-panel.md`](docs/operations/ec2-panel.md), [`docs/contributing.md`](docs/contributing.md), [`scripts/ec2_app_deploy.sh`](scripts/ec2_app_deploy.sh):

**Add (placeholders only in docs):**

- `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`
- `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`
- `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` — e.g. `https://kuchup.com/api/auth/google/callback` (and MCP callback if separate host)
- `PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS` — e.g. `you@gmail.com`

**Remove / stop documenting:** `PANEL_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, password bootstrap, [`scripts/reset_password.py`](scripts/reset_password.py) + [`relocation_jobs/reset_password.py`](relocation_jobs/reset_password.py)

**Keep:** `PANEL_ALLOW_REGISTER`, `PANEL_SECRET_KEY`

Google Cloud Console: OAuth client (Web), authorized redirect URIs for panel (+ MCP public base if callback lives there).

## Tests

- Replace `auth_client` password login with `session_transaction` seeding `user_id` / `username`, or a test helper that inserts a Google user then sets session
- Session env: drop `PANEL_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; set `PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS`, fake `GOOGLE_CLIENT_*`
- Unit-test `login_or_register_google`: create when flag on; reject when flag off; admin email → `is_admin`
- Mock token verify in `google_oauth` for callback route tests
- Update MCP OAuth tests to complete login without password form
- Run once after the unit of work: `pytest tests -o addopts=`

## Implementation order

1. Schema migration + repo upsert APIs
2. `google_oauth.py` + `auth.py` rewrite (delete password paths)
3. Panel routes + UI
4. MCP Google login + shared upsert
5. Env/docs/deploy cleanup; delete reset-password
6. Test fixture + new/updated tests

## Skills / standards applied

- **codebase-memory** first for call graph; thin routes, SQL only in repo
- **engineering-standards / rules.md**: top-level imports, delete dead password code, no secrets in docs
- **module-layout**: types/rules then helpers then public API; keep functions short (authorize / exchange / upsert / callback as separate functions)
- **design.md**: single Google CTA, brand lockup, orange primary pill — no marketing enrichment on app login
- **collaboration**: structural choice fixed here — Google helpers live in `core/google_oauth.py`, not a new top-level domain package

Add core/google_oauth.py; rewrite core/auth.py for Google-only + PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS + PANEL_ALLOW_REGISTER
Google start/callback routes; remove login/register password APIs; login panel UI + auth.js
MCP oauth_pages Google flow sharing login_or_register_google
Update .env.example, EC2 deploy/docs; delete reset_password; remove PANEL_ADMIN_PASSWORD
Fix conftest auth_client + add Google register/admin/flag + MCP tests; run pytest tests

content.text: Important finding: the SQS doc we have is **not** plan-based opportunity delivery — it’s fetch/PDF queueing. Your monetized personalization layer isn’t written yet, so I need two product choices before expanding the plan.

You’re right that Google login alone is the wrong unit of work. Identity has to sit under a **commercial entitlement + personalized opportunity** model.

### Gap vs existing docs
[`docs/reference/multi-user-scaling-proposal.md`](docs/reference/multi-user-scaling-proposal.md) uses SQS for **fetch / PDF / board-projection jobs** (infra scaling). It does **not** define “push matched opportunities by paid plan.”

[`homepage/app/pricing/page.tsx`](homepage/app/pricing/page.tsx) only has marketing placeholders (Free Preview vs Full Access “coming soon”). There is **no** plan schema, Stripe, board gating, or MCP quota in code.

Today a logged-in user gets the **full catalog** plus their tracking overlay — not a monetized subset.

### What the expanded plan must cover
1. **Identity** — Google-only signup (your 1C/2C)
2. **Plans / money** — entitlements on the user (free vs paid, grandfathering)
3. **Opportunity visibility** — what each plan may see (not the whole catalog)
4. **Async delivery** — SQS (or related workers) for matching / fan-out / projection refresh
5. **MCP quotas** — request limits and tool access by plan
6. **Scaling SQS** — keep the existing fetch/PDF queue work as a separate infra track

Two decisions lock the architecture:

**1. How should “not all opportunities” work for a logged-in free user?**
- **A. Cap** — same catalog shape, but only N newest / featured roles (or N companies)
- **B. Preference match** — user sets countries / seniority / keywords; board is filtered to matches; paid unlocks broader/full catalog
- **C. Unlock gate** — free Google account can sign in but board stays locked / preview-sized until paid (closest to current pricing copy)
- **D. Hybrid** — free = preference-matched + hard cap; paid = full catalog + higher MCP limits

**2. Billing for v1 of this system?**
- **A. Stripe subscriptions** in the same program (checkout + webhooks → plan on user)
- **B. Entitlement stubs first** — `plan` / quotas in DB + admin override; wire Stripe later
- **C. Manual / invite paid** — you set plan in DB/admin; no self-serve checkout yet

My recommendation for a shippable first cut: **1D + 2B** — hybrid visibility + entitlement model now, Stripe after the gates work end-to-end (board + MCP). SQS then does two jobs: (infra) fetch/PDF as already proposed, and (product) async “recompute this user’s opportunity set when catalog or plan changes.”

Reply with e.g. `1D 2B` (or your variants) and I’ll rewrite the Cursor plan into that full product architecture.

# Personalized opportunities via Google identity + plans

## Problem

Google signup alone is insufficient. Once many users register:

- Showing the **full catalog** to every logged-in user destroys differentiation and monetization.
- MCP (CV reframe, PDF) must be **quota-limited** on free and unlocked (or higher) on paid.
- Opportunity sets must be **recomputed asynchronously** when the shared catalog changes or when a user’s plan/preferences change — not only filtered ad hoc on each HTTP read forever.

Existing docs cover **infra** SQS ([`docs/reference/multi-user-scaling-proposal.md`](docs/reference/multi-user-scaling-proposal.md): fetch/PDF/projection performance) and **marketing** placeholders ([`homepage/app/pricing/page.tsx`](homepage/app/pricing/page.tsx)). They do **not** yet define plan-based opportunity delivery. This plan is that product layer, with Google auth as Phase A.

## Decisions (locked)

| Topic | Choice |
|-------|--------|
| Signup | Self-serve Google login, gated by `PANEL_ALLOW_REGISTER` (**1C**) |
| Password | Removed everywhere — panel, MCP, admin bootstrap (**2C**) |
| Admin | `PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS` → `is_admin` (admins bypass commercial caps) |
| Opportunity model | **Hybrid 1D** — free = preference-matched + hard cap; paid/`full` = full catalog (scoped by prefs countries) + higher MCP limits |
| Billing v1 | **Entitlement stubs 2B** — `plan` in DB + admin override; no checkout in Phases A–E |
| Payments later | **NOWPayments** (Phase F) — crypto/fiat checkout + IPN upgrades `plan`; not Stripe |
| SQS product use | Queue `user-opportunity-refresh` to rebuild each user’s visible opportunity set |
| SQS infra use | Keep fetch/PDF queues as a **parallel** track (Phase G), per multi-user-scaling proposal |

## Target architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  google[Google_OAuth] --> identity[users_identity]
  identity --> entitlements[user_entitlements]
  prefs[user_preferences] --> matcher[opportunity_matcher]
  catalog[shared_catalog] --> matcher
  entitlements --> matcher
  matcher --> projection[user_opportunities]
  projection --> boardAPI[GET_api_board]
  entitlements --> mcpGate[MCP_quota_gate]
  catalogSync[catalog_sync] --> sqsRefresh[SQS_opportunity_refresh]
  entitlements --> sqsRefresh
  prefs --> sqsRefresh
  sqsRefresh --> matcher
  nowpay[NOWPayments_later] --> entitlements
```

**Read path:** panel and MCP never “see the whole world.” They read `user_opportunities` (or equivalent projection) already filtered by plan + preferences. Tracking overlay (apply/reject/…) still merges on top as today ([`docs/reference/catalog-pattern.md`](docs/reference/catalog-pattern.md)).

**Write path for money (later):** NOWPayments IPN → set `plan=full` (+ expiry if needed) → enqueue opportunity refresh.

---

## Phase A — Google-only identity

Same technical cut as before; foundation only.

- Schema: `google_sub`, `email`, `display_name`; drop `password_hash`
- [`relocation_jobs/core/google_oauth.py`](relocation_jobs/core/google_oauth.py) + rewrite [`core/auth.py`](relocation_jobs/core/auth.py)
- Routes: `/api/auth/google`, `/api/auth/google/callback`; delete login/register password APIs
- Panel UI: single **Continue with Google** CTA ([`design.md`](design.md))
- MCP OAuth page: same Google tunnel → `complete_login_redirect`
- Env: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_*`, `PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS`; remove `PANEL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` / `reset_password`
- New Google users default to `plan=free` (Phase B column; if B not yet shipped, add nullable plan with default in A)

---

## Phase B — Entitlement stubs (no payment yet)

### Plans

| Plan | Board | MCP | Notes |
|------|-------|-----|-------|
| `free` | Preference match + hard caps | Low daily tool quota | Default for new Google users |
| `full` | Full catalog within preference countries (or all countries if prefs empty and paid) | High / unlimited soft cap | Paid / early-access |
| `grandfathered` | Same as `full` | Same as `full` | Marketing promise; admin-set |
| `is_admin` | Bypass all commercial caps | Bypass | Ops |

Concrete free caps (env-tunable, defaults locked for v1):

- `FREE_BOARD_COMPANY_CAP=25` — max companies in the personalized set per country scope
- `FREE_MCP_DAILY_REQUESTS=20` — counted MCP tool invocations per UTC day
- `FULL_MCP_DAILY_REQUESTS=500` (or `0` = unlimited)

### Schema (SQL only in repo / migrations)

On `users` or sibling `user_entitlements` (prefer **columns on `users`** for v1 to avoid join tax):

- `plan TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free'`
- `plan_updated_at TEXT`
- `mcp_quota_date TEXT` / `mcp_quota_used INTEGER` (daily bucket)
- Optional later: `plan_expires_at` for time-boxed full access

Admin API (existing admin surface): `PATCH` plan for a user (grandfather / grant full without payment).

`GET /api/auth/status` exposes `{ plan, board_cap, mcp_remaining }` so the UI can show upgrade CTAs.

### MCP gate

In MCP HTTP/tool entry ([`relocation_jobs/mcp/`](relocation_jobs/mcp/)): before expensive tools (reframe, PDF, save tailored), call `consume_mcp_quota(user_id)`. Free over quota → clear error pointing to pricing / upgrade. Admins bypass.

---

## Phase C — Preferences (personalization inputs)

New preference store (table `user_preferences` or JSON on user):

- `target_countries` — list of country keys (required for free match to work)
- `seniority` — e.g. mid / senior / staff (optional)
- `keywords` — short include list (optional)
- `remote_ok` — bool

**Onboarding:** after first Google login, if prefs empty → lightweight panel step (countries multi-select at minimum) before full board. Paid users can skip or set later.

No ML in v1 — deterministic filters against catalog fields already used by the board (country, title keywords, location/remote tags).

---

## Phase D — Personalized board reads

Change the contract of [`GET /api/board`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/board.py) (and remote board if applicable):

1. Resolve entitlement + prefs for `g.user_id`.
2. Load **allowed opportunity keys** from `user_opportunities` (Phase E builds this). Until E ships, a **sync fallback matcher** in service layer is acceptable for low N, then deleted when SQS refresh is reliable.
3. Flatten/merge tracking only for allowed companies/jobs — same [`panel/flatten.py`](relocation_jobs/panel/) semantics, smaller input set.
4. Free users hitting the cap see an explicit “Upgrade for full board” affordance (pricing link), not a silent empty board.

**Public** surfaces stay preview-only (unchanged marketing model). Authenticated ≠ entitled to everything.

This aligns with (and can later feed) [`board-read-model-proposal.md`](docs/reference/board-read-model-proposal.md): projection rows become **entitlement-aware**, not a full-catalog clone per user.

---

## Phase E — SQS opportunity refresh (product queue)

Distinct from fetch/PDF queues.

| Queue | Producer | Consumer |
|-------|----------|----------|
| `user-opportunity-refresh` | Catalog sync complete; plan change; prefs save; admin grant | Worker runs matcher → upserts `user_opportunities` |
| DLQ | Redrive after N fails | Ops review |

Payload: `{ user_id }` or `{ country }` (fan-out: country catalog change → enqueue all users with that country in prefs; cap fan-out with batching).

Module layout (mirrors scaling proposal):

- `relocation_jobs/core/sqs_client.py` — boto3, env-gated

- Failure modes: unpaid, underpaid, expired invoice — leave user on `free`
